name: Hypergraph Node Classification and Regression
problem_statement: Train or evaluate a declared hypergraph neural model to predict vertex labels or targets while preserving hyperedge incidence.

normalization: Preserve every hyperedge incidence set and vertex ID.
Reject repeated vertices inside one hyperedge.

problem_inputs.name: target_key
problem_inputs.description: Ground-truth vertex attribute available only in permitted splits.

problem_inputs.name: split_key
problem_inputs.description: Attribute assigning train, validation, test, or inference vertices.

problem_inputs.name: model
problem_inputs.description: Declared architecture, hyperparameters, preprocessing and checkpoint.

required_outputs.name: predictions
required_outputs.description: Targets or class probabilities for requested vertices.

required_outputs.name: model_artifact
required_outputs.description: Model parameters/checkpoint reference and reproducible hyperparameters.

required_outputs.name: split_metrics
required_outputs.description: Metrics with denominators and explicit split membership.

solution_semantics.objective: Train or evaluate a declared hypergraph neural model to predict vertex labels or targets while preserving hyperedge incidence.
solution_semantics.exactness: Statistical learning with declared split, seed and tolerance; no deterministic optimum claim.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each external vertex ID occurs once; output multiplicities follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering among equally valid solutions is required.

validation_rules: Retain hyperedges and incidence IDs; any clique or mediator expansion must be declared as a model transformation.
Only training labels influence fitting; validation selects hyperparameters and test labels are held out.
Verify prediction dimensions, finite outputs and classification probability normalization.
Reproduce inference on a small hypergraph using the same parameters; do not require trained models to have identical accuracy.
edge_cases: Singleton hyperedges and isolated vertices are legal with a declared model convention.
Variable-size hyperedges cannot be silently replaced by ordinary pairwise edges.
